title: add support for compression of capture file by gzip
description:
add support for compression of capture file by gzip

* add --compress-type option to choose compression type.
* add radio button to choose compression type to Wireshark.

This is a series of 4 patches, the initial patch that adds the feature and then three patches that does incremental fixes for that patch.
This makes it hard to review because an issue in one patch might already be fixed in a later patch.

So instead, since the latter three patches are all fixes to the initial patch you should merge these 4 patches into one single patch.


That said, there are a few issues still in ringbuffer.c with trailing spaces as well as code style ('{' does not go on a line ow its own)

Otherwise I have tested the patch and it seems to be working nicely.
I like the attention to detail you into the "compress" checkbox and that it defaults to the state of the file we originally read into wireshark.

Could you use this as a teaching moment and explain "merge these 4 patches into one single patch"?  
I've got a couple MRs - !440 !180 !524 - that contain several changes. Where can I do better?  
("do better" in the gitlab process)

Use :

git rebase -i HEAD~5

Then in the editor you can tell git "fold this patch into the previous" patch.
If you want to avoid multiple commits in the first place you can use `git commit --amend` to update the current commit instead of creating a new one.

Sorry for the late reply, I didn't notice you had replied, @sahlberg.

I rebased from latest master, squash four commits and fix brackets coding style.

> I like the attention to detail you into the "compress" checkbox and that it defaults to the state of the file we originally read into wireshark.

This is, as far as I can tell, for live captures, so what's "the file we originally read into wireshark" here?
Ah, sorry, I got confused. That part has been there already.
